newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels to repeat skating rink success.
newsitem.headline: Brussels to repeat skating rink success.

text.p: The ice skating rink set up for the first time at Christmas and the New Year in Brussels' famed central square was such a success that it will be repeated this year, city Mayor Francois-Xavier de Donnea said on Thursday.

Some 19,000 skaters were among the 150,000 people who visited the rennaissance Grand Place between December 20 and January 5 -- a time when business in the area normally grinds to a halt and petty crime booms, de Donnea told a news conference.
"We set ourselves four main objectives and achieved them all," he said.

"We gave Grand Place back to the people of Brussels. The media coverage we got was excellent for our international image. We boosted trade for the local businesses, particularly the cafes, and we entertained 150,000 people".
Equally important, de Donnea said, was that the event only cost the city of Brussels 60,000 francs ($2,000) -- the rest of the 11 million franc ($366,000) tab being picked up by an array of sponsors.
This year the 800 square metre ice rink -- containing 64 tonnes of ice -- will be moved to the top of the square and increased in size.
Again one hour of skating will cost just 100 francs ($3) including the hire of skates, and the range of ice spectaculars and events will all be free.
"At that time of the year normally nobody comes to Grand Place. Many businesses close down and there is a lot of crime.
"This year everybody came, businesses did well and there was no more crime than on a usual weekend or Friday night," De Donnea said.

He said the only criticism of the rink was that it had been too small and people had not always had a good view of the shows -- both of which would be addressed when the rink is recreated next December 19 for two weeks.
"We were very lucky with the weather this time. It could have rained for the entire two weeks -- although I have to say it was very cold out there," de Donnea said.
The temperature in Brussels went down to minus 16 degrees Celsius at one stage during the two weeks as northern Europe shivered in Siberian winds and polar temperatures.
